newsitem.title: USA: Petrobras sees '97 oil output at 1m bpd, more ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras sees '97 oil output at 1m bpd, more ADRs.

text.p: Brazilian state oil company Petrobras expects oil output to rise by 100,000 barrels a day (bpd) to a million barrels next year, a senior company finance official said Wednesday.
The company is aiming to issue "level-three" American Depository Receipts (ADRs) to raise capital, according to Daniel Oliveira, finance manager for Petrobras.
Petrobras said in mid-October that it sees oil output for 1996 up by 16 percent on the previous year at nearly 900,000 bpd of oil equivalent.

Oliveira didn't specify from where the increased output would come but Petrobras recently has had success in offshore exploratory drilling and recently reported a potentially large find in the Campos Basin off the Rio de Janeiro coast which could add between 430 million and 640 million barrels to Brazil's 1995 proved reserves level of 4.8 billion barrels of oil.
The company also is on track to open up its oil sector to private foreign investment, despite political bickering which has delayed necessary legislation originally expected to be passed last summer.

The Brazilian government must pass legislation to specify how Petrobras's monopoly will be broken up and Oliviera, speaking at a Salomon Brothers conference on Latin America, said that he expects it by the middle of next year. The disagreement between government and Congress has centered on how the state oil company will be regulated.

"We think the company (Petrobras) could be much more profitable if it is freed from ties to the government," he said. Petrobras believes that through increased competition it can boost oil production and profitability, he said.

Oliviera said the company would work toward issuing a level-3 ADR issue by the end of this year, even though it only had approval currently for a level-1 issue. "There is a decision to go up a level-3 (ADR issue)."
The level-3 issue would allow the company to raise totally new capital through an issue, including a U.S. placement. A Petrobras spokesman in Brazil could not confirm the plans.
The government said last month it plans to sell more than a third of the voting share capital it holds in the company.
Meanwhile, Petrobras plans to issue a further $125 million in bonds, probably denominated in Japanese yen, but possibly in Italian lira, by year end, Oliviera said.

External borrowings will should run at $500-$600 million next year, compared with $500 international bond issuance million by the end of 1996, and the company would pursue a diversified strategy, Oliviera said.
